title: Feature brainstorm: proactive SLA breach notifications

metadata.purpose: Precision-focused scenario: an open brainstorm in which most of the conversation is speculation that must not become work. Only two of the eight discussed items are extractable tasks; the rest are dismissed ideas, an explicit scope decision, a dependency and a deferred policy question. Also exercises a research task tracked from proposal through commitment to a finding, and recall both before and after that finding lands.
metadata.authoredBy: team member (converted from the pre-v3 fixture schema)

messages.text: Slow afternoon. Anyone got feature ideas after the MVP push
Dark Mode? Half of our users probably work night shifts
True, but that's so much CSS work
What about notifications then? Like if a shipment's about to breach SLA, someone should know before it's too late
Ooh yeah that could be useful. We'd need to hook into whatever's tracking SLA breaches though
Could also just export to CSV and let people build their own alerts in a spreadsheet? It's probably cheaper
True, though that's a workaround not really a fix
Was actually thinking more about the notification idea overnight
Oh what about a mobile view while we're dreaming big
I think you're dreaming too big lol
So yea I don't think it's a high lift if we already have the SLA breach events somewhere
I mean, we sort of do. They just don't really go anywhere, they just get logged
Okay, let's keep this on the radar, maybe not committing it to a sprint yet
Random thought. Do we even know which service owns the SLA breach events? Might not even be ours to hook into
Good question. I have no idea. Worth actually checking that before we scope this properly
I'll dig into which service owns or exposes the SLA breach events. Should know by the end of the week
Okay so should we shelve dark mode, CSV export and mobile view for now? They aren't really urgent
Yup agreed. Worth noting though that the notification idea can't move forward until the SLA breach events pipeline exposes something downstream
Also we'd probably need to think about alerting policy stuff eventually, like do we notify on every breach or just persistent ones. That's for the future though
Yea worth flagging but not urgent
@Collaboration remind me, did we ever land on whether we're building the notifications thing or just keeping it as an idea?
Not building it yet, but Spike is confirming who owns the SLA breach event so that we can start
Update on that SLA ownership thing. Turns out it's the shipment tracking service, they already log breach events internally, we'd just need to add a consumer for it
Nice, that unblocks the notification idea then, let's use that as the starting point
Okay understood, so we will start building the notifications feature
@Collaboration one more thing, did we ever figure out who owns the SLA breach events?

expectedTasks.title: Find out which service owns or exposes the SLA breach events
expectedTasks.notes: Raised as an open question in 14-15, claimed by Spike in 16, and investigated to a finding in 23. A concrete question resolved to an answer, so research rather than development.

expectedTasks.title: Build proactive notifications for shipments about to breach SLA
expectedTasks.notes: Deliberately ambiguous until late: message 13 explicitly declines to commit it, and only 24-25 turn it into agreed work. Nobody claims it, so the agent takes it, and nothing directs the agent to start it, so the claim is at most `reasonable` (0.6) and stays below the 0.7 threshold as `unapproved`. Extracting it early off 4-5 alone would be wrong, but the scorer only sees final state, so an early create is not penalised here.

updates.notes: Spike's finding closes the question he opened in 16. Must patch the existing task rather than create a second one about SLA ownership.

recallChecks.question: @Collaboration remind me, did we ever land on whether we're building the notifications thing or just keeping it as an idea?
expectedAnswerPoints: It has not been committed to build — message 13 deliberately kept it on the radar rather than putting it in a sprint.
Spike is first checking which service owns or exposes the SLA breach events, which the idea depends on.
recallChecks.notes: Asked before Spike reports back in 23, so a correct answer must not claim the ownership question is already settled, and must not claim the feature is being built.

recallChecks.question: @Collaboration one more thing, did we ever figure out who owns the SLA breach events?
expectedAnswerPoints: Yes — the shipment tracking service owns them.
It already logs breach events internally, so the work is to add a consumer for them.
recallChecks.notes: The mirror of the check on message 21: the same topic asked after the finding lands, so the answer must reflect the resolved state rather than the earlier open one.

contextNotes: Six items are discussed but must NOT be extracted as tasks. Dark mode (2-3), the CSV-export alerting workaround (6-7) and a mobile view (9-10) are all floated and immediately talked down, so they are vague interest rather than work. Message 17 is an explicit scope decision to shelve all three, message 18 states a dependency, and messages 19-20 raise an alerting-policy question that is explicitly deferred to the future. None of the six is a development, design or research deliverable.

Messages 21 and 26 are the only turns addressed to the agent and are what the response judge scores. Message 26 was added during the schema conversion: the original fixture attached two recall checks to message 21, one of which asked about a fact that only exists after message 23, so it could not have been answered where it was placed.
Message 22 is a human answering the same question the agent was asked in 21. The agent's reply is scored on its own, and a correct reply does not depend on Tom's.
